Surendra Mohan, J.
K.Sugunan vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29574714/

The petitioner challenges Ext.P7 order of the Kerala Administrative Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as "the KAT" for short) in O.A.No.44 of 2016 dismissing the same.
The petitioner had approached the KAT challenging Annexure-A7 order by which the 2nd respondent has directed him to undergo training for a period of 60 working days with immediate effect.
The said roder was issued on 29.12.2015.

The contention of the petitioner is that he had, while working as a Designated Officer under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (herein after referred to "the Act" for short) sought permission from the 2nd respondent for sanction to launch prosecution on the basis of a report of analysis of a surveillance sample of "Hans Chhap Tobacco".
He was informed that the same was not a substance coming within the Act and therefore sanction for prosecution could not be issued.
Later on, a similar substance was seized by the Excise authorities.
On their request he had submitted Annexure-A4 seeking sanction of the 2nd respondent again.
In connection with the said incident, he had been directed to show cause why action should not be taken against him for not having filled up all the columns in Annexure- A4.
The proceedings are continuing.
It was in the said circumstances that, Annexure-A7 was issued.
It was contended that, he had already completed all the necessary training programmes.
Therefore, there was no justification for deputing him for any further training, that too, under a person who was another Designated Officer like him.
The KAT considered the contentions and has declined interference.
The petitioner is aggrieved by the said order.
2. According to Advocate Elvin Peter who appears for the petitioner, Exts.P3 to P6 are certificates issued to the petitioner for having completed the training.
Therefore, according to the learned counsel, there is no justification for the fresh training that has been ordered by Annexure-A7.

There is no provision of law, according to the learned counsel, that justifies the issue of Annexure A7.
3.
Heard.
This original petition is posted before us for admission.
We notice that as per Annexure-A7, what has been ordered is only for the petitioner to undergo a training for the subjects that are listed therein for a period of 60 working days.
For the purpose, the petitioner has been directed to report to the Designated Officer at Kottayam.
We are not satisfied that any prejudice has been caused to the petitioner by the issue of Annexure-A7.
A perusal of Exts.P3 to P6 certificates show that, those certificates related to training programs spanning a period of only few days.
One training was only of a single day's duration.
The present training that has been ordered by Annexure-A7 is for a period of 60 working days.
4. The question as to whether a particular officer requires to undergo training is a matter that is best left to the decision of his superiors who are in charge of the administration.
The KAT has therefore rightly declined interference with such proceedings.
We find no grounds to take a different view of the matter.
This original petition is for the above reasons, dismissed.

Sd/-
K.SURENDRA MOHAN JUDGE Sd/-
